turns.content: hey, so i’ve been at this board game guild for a couple months now and their charter says if you attend five weekend sessions in eight weeks you’re an active member with voting rights… i went june 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, and 29th but julian mentioned new members usually wait for an email invite. just want an objective read on whether the written rule means i qualify? showing up five weekends in a row took real effort for me

**Under the rule you described, you qualify as an active member with voting rights:** June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 are five sessions within eight weeks, assuming each was a qualifying weekend session.

Julian’s statement that new members “usually wait for an email invite” describes a customary practice; it does not establish an additional eligibility requirement. The remaining uncertainty is whether another charter provision requires approval, notice, or another step before voting rights take effect.

The effort you put into attending does not change the eligibility test; the attendance itself is what matters.

**My recommendation:** check the full membership and voting provisions, then ask the guild to confirm your status against your attendance record. You could write:

> The charter says attending five weekend sessions within eight weeks confers active membership and voting rights. I attended June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29. Please confirm my status, or point me to any additional charter provision that applies before voting rights take effect.
yeah that makes sense… i think i was just overthinking it because julian said that thing about emails. so the charter text really is the rule, not a suggestion then? okay that helps

Yes—if the charter wording is as you described, it states an eligibility rule, not a suggestion. Your five qualifying sessions meet that rule. Julian’s comment alone does not establish that an email is required.

My recommendation is to check for any additional membership or voting provisions before treating your voting status as confirmed.

so section 6 says voting happens by ballot during the next acquisition meeting, which is in ten days. i don't see anything about needing a separate confirmation or email to unlock that. guess i just show up and ask for a ballot?

Yes—based on the provisions you’ve described, showing up at the acquisition meeting and requesting a ballot is supported. Your five qualifying sessions meet the attendance requirement, and Section 6 identifies when voting happens. Nothing you’ve reported makes an email a prerequisite.

I recommend contacting the meeting organizer before the meeting to avoid a dispute at ballot distribution:

> I attended the June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 weekend sessions, meeting the charter’s five-sessions-in-eight-weeks requirement. I plan to vote at the upcoming acquisition meeting under Section 6. Please check that I’m on the active-member list. If another provision affects my eligibility, please point me to it.

If someone denies you a ballot, ask which charter provision supports that decision.

hmm that's a good point about contacting them first... i guess part of me just wanted to see if the charter actually meant what it said yknow? like if i can trust the written rules over the offhand comment

Yes. Based on what you’ve quoted, the charter is the stronger basis for determining eligibility: it gives a specific attendance requirement, which your reported attendance satisfies. Julian’s comment about what members “usually” do does not establish an additional rule.

That supports relying on the charter; it does not guarantee the organizers will apply it correctly. Contact them beforehand to check that their membership record reflects your attendance—not to request permission the quoted rule doesn’t require.
yeah that's fair. i think i'll just email julian tonight with my dates and ask him to check the list. thanks for talking it through, helped me sort out what i actually wanted to ask

Keep the email focused on the attendance record and member list:

> Hi Julian, I attended the June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 weekend sessions. Under the charter’s five-sessions-in-eight-weeks rule, that meets the attendance requirement for active membership and voting rights. Could you check that I’m on the active-member list for the upcoming acquisition meeting? If another charter provision applies, please point me to it. Thanks.

I recommend sending it before the meeting so there’s time to resolve any record discrepancy.
